summary:
BEYOND ORBIT is an interactive 2D pixel-art space mission simulation that transforms the complexity of space exploration into an engaging, educational experience.

Inspired by NASA's Artemis program, players take the role of Ryan Blake, an astronaut preparing for a mission to the Moon. From astronaut training and pre-launch mission planning to spacecraft operations, orbital maneuvers, and lunar landing, players experience the challenges of managing a space mission.

The game features interactive spacecraft systems, resource management, trajectory planning, engineering decisions, crew interactions, and dynamic mission emergencies. Every decision carries consequences: poor resource allocation, incorrect maneuvers, or system failures can jeopardize mission success.

Drawing on NASA's mission-design resources and systems-engineering principles, BEYOND ORBIT introduces players to real aerospace concepts through accessible, simplified gameplay.

Our goal is to demonstrate that successful space exploration requires more than reaching a destination—it requires planning, teamwork, adaptability, and informed engineering decisions.
details:
BEYOND ORBIT is an interactive, story-driven 2D space mission simulator developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge by Team 404: Earth Not Found.

Inspired by NASA's Artemis program, the game places players in the role of Ryan Blake, a mission specialist preparing for a journey to the Moon. Rather than simply watching a spacecraft launch, players participate in astronaut training, mission preparation, spacecraft operations, engineering decisions, and orbital maneuvers.

How the Game Works

The experience begins at a NASA-inspired facility, where players complete medical assessments, simulation exercises, and mission preparations before boarding their spacecraft.

After launch, players explore the spacecraft and interact with four operational terminals:

  • Cockpit: Monitor flight status, prepare maneuvers, and execute engine burns.
  • Engineering: Manage electrical power, propulsion systems, and equipment failures.
  • Medical & Storage: Monitor crew health and manage oxygen, food, water, and supplies.
  • Navigation & Communications: Plan trajectories, calculate course corrections, and communicate with Mission Control.

Throughout the journey, players encounter mission events requiring decisions under limited time and resources. These decisions affect spacecraft conditions, crew safety, and mission success. Incorrect maneuvers, excessive fuel consumption, and critical system failures can result in mission failure.

The current playable experience progresses through lunar-orbit insertion, with lunar landing and the return journey forming the planned continuation.

Technologies and Development

BEYOND ORBIT was developed using Unity 6 and C#, with custom 2D pixel-art environments, character sprites, interactive interfaces, dialogue systems, and gameplay mechanics.

The game's visual identity, called OrbitPixel, combines cinematic storytelling with carefully designed pixel art, making complex aerospace concepts accessible without overwhelming players.

NASA Resources and Scientific Foundation

Our design draws on NASA's Design and Develop Science Missions resource and its systems-engineering approach, emphasizing the relationships between spacecraft systems, mission objectives, and operational constraints.

NASA's Mission Design Lab, General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT), and mission-visualization resources also provide conceptual references for engineering trade-offs, trajectory planning, and mission operations.

The game uses simplified educational models rather than claiming to reproduce NASA's high-fidelity mission simulations.

Creativity and Educational Impact

BEYOND ORBIT combines narrative storytelling, interactive exploration, engineering simulations, and consequential decision-making.

Instead of presenting scientific information through conventional lessons, the game encourages players to learn through experimentation, failure, and improvement.

Its central lesson is that successful space missions require balancing competing demands: fuel, power, resources, safety, navigation, and mission objectives.

BEYOND ORBIT transforms space mission engineering from an abstract subject into an interactive experience where every decision matters.
